original_source: US-WEST1: Multiple cloud products experiencing network issues
failure_pattern: A routine SDN maintenance event triggered a failover that used a corrupted checkpoint lacking configuration data. The corrupted configuration was propagated to 15% of network switches in us‑west1‑b, and a race condition in the switch firmware caused those switches to crash. The resulting switch failures caused widespread packet loss, latency, and unresponsive instances across multiple GCP services.
mitigation_principle: disable triggering SDN feature; improve test coverage; validate checkpoint data before persistence; enhance maintenance safety checks; redistribute SDN services to limit blast radius; develop pre-deployment validation components; improve switch recovery tooling; enhance monitoring for faster detection

original_source: Multiple GCP products are experiencing Service issues.
symptoms: intermittent API and UI access issues

failure_pattern: A code change in the Service Control system introduced a policy update with blank fields, causing a null pointer exception that crashed the API management binaries globally. The crash propagated through the distributed infrastructure, leading to 503 and 5xx errors for external API requests and downstream services. The lack of randomized exponential backoff caused cascading restarts, overloading regions such as us-central1 and prolonging recovery.
mitigation_principle: freeze changes to critical stacks during deployment; deploy fail‑safe red‑button to disable faulty paths; modularize components to fail open; enforce feature flags for critical changes; improve static analysis and testing; audit systems consuming globally replicated data; implement incremental data propagation; ensure randomized exponential backoff on restarts; enhance external communication and monitoring resilience

original_source: Multiple services impacted in australia-southeast1.

The loss of power to the affected rows cascaded across the zone, disabling critical infrastructure and leading to widespread service disruptions across multiple GCP services.
mitigation_principle: Audit and update ATS settings to match load and design; perform comprehensive operational procedure audit; collaborate with utility provider to investigate power events; verify redundant power path protection; implement automated monitoring of ATS trip thresholds; conduct regular power resilience testing

failure_pattern: A code change in the Traffic Director configuration pipeline assumed all customer configurations had been migrated to a new format. Because the migration was incomplete, the pipeline incorrectly deleted some configurations, deprogramming downstream clients. This caused Traffic Director‑managed backends to lose configuration, leading to HTTP 500 errors on load balancers.
mitigation_principle: Implement comprehensive migration validation checks; add automated rollback on migration failure; enhance monitoring and alerting for configuration changes; perform thorough code review and testing before deployment

original_source: Google Cloud Networking connectivity issue for approximately 20 minutes.
failure_pattern: A configuration change in the networking infrastructure introduced incorrect routing or ACL settings, causing transient connectivity disruptions across multiple regions and services. The change propagated to the global networking fabric, leading to widespread connectivity loss for VPC and hybrid connectivity users. The issue was resolved once the configuration was rolled back.
mitigation_principle: enhanced validation of configuration changes; automated configuration drift detection; improved monitoring for early detection; rollback procedures; change management review

original_source: Google Compute Engine, Persistent Disk, Virtual Private Cloud are experiencing issues in us-east4-a
failure_pattern: A power loss event caused the primary power to the affected racks to drop, and the backup power transition failed, leaving hardware offline. This resulted in compute hosts, persistent disks, and VPC hosts becoming unavailable, causing VM interruptions, stuck I/O operations, and high latency for affected workloads.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant power supplies and robust failover mechanisms; regularly test backup power transitions; monitor power status and alert on failures; design systems for graceful degradation during power loss

original_source: Multiple Cloud products impacted in europe-west9-c zone
symptoms: job stalls in streaming and batch processing
admin operations unavailable for Cloud Bigtable
root_cause_category: electrical failure in cooling control system
failure_pattern: An electrical fault in the cooling control system caused the cooling infrastructure in the europe-west9-c zone to fail, leading to insufficient cooling. To prevent hardware damage, the engineering team proactively shut down physical machines, which in turn caused multiple Google Cloud services to become unavailable for customers.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant cooling control systems; monitor cooling system health and temperature thresholds; establish automated fail-safes and alerts for environmental controls; conduct regular testing of cooling system resilience; enforce proactive shutdown protocols with minimal service disruption

original_source: Multiple Google Cloud Platform services impacted globally with operational latency
failure_pattern: A configuration change in the control plane infrastructure introduced elevated latency and failures. This latency propagated across the distributed control plane, causing API calls to time out and operations such as instance creation, deletion, and backups to fail globally. The cascading effect impacted multiple GCP services worldwide.
mitigation_principle: implement rigorous validation checks for control plane configurations; enhance monitoring and alerting for latency anomalies; enforce automated rollback on configuration changes; conduct thorough testing before deployment; maintain a change approval process

original_source: Multiple Google Cloud services in the europe-west9-a zone are impacted
root_cause_category: physical infrastructure failure leading to quorum loss
failure_pattern: A water leak caused a fire and forced an emergency power shutdown of one of the three buildings in the europe-west9 region. The loss of power to two of the three Spanner replicas in that building caused a quorum loss, which cascaded into control plane outages and global fanout API failures, disrupting many services.
mitigation_principle: ensure fault‑tolerant replica placement across independent buildings; implement automated health checks for power and environmental sensors; establish rapid isolation and shutdown procedures; improve fire suppression and water intrusion detection; regularly audit infrastructure risk and update playbooks; parallelize recovery processes; enhance IAM policy sync times; test zonal/regional failure scenarios

original_source: Multiple cloud products are experiencing networking issues in us-central1
failure_pattern: A management plane change intended to improve API update processing triggered an unexpected increase in memory usage on the virtual network router control plane in us-central1. The resulting out‑of‑memory crashes caused the controllers to restart repeatedly, preventing timely updates to router state. This synchronized failure across all zonal routers caused packet loss and delayed networking for newly created VMs, leading to failed VM creations, cluster operation delays, and other service disruptions.
mitigation_principle: implement proactive memory risk alerting; refactor deployment configurations for faster memory reallocation; re‑evaluate API reconciliation safety mechanisms; improve cross‑team visibility of management plane changes; adjust deployment footprints to reduce regional memory exhaustion risks; optimize memory usage in traffic routers and controllers

original_source: Virtual Private Cloud public IP packet loss affecting GCE instances in multiple regions
failure_pattern: A configuration change to a load balancer incorrectly routed traffic for VM public IPs to a wrong data plane component. This misdirection caused elevated packet loss and latency across VPC, Cloud NAT, and Cloud VPN services in the affected regions.
mitigation_principle: implement automated configuration validation; enforce peer review and change approval processes; deploy configuration drift detection; perform impact analysis before changes; establish rapid rollback procedures

original_source: All the impacted GCP products in australia-southeast2 have recovered.
failure_pattern: A voltage swell event caused the UPS to boost voltage beyond the tolerance of the networking devices, triggering protective shutdowns. The resulting device reboots disrupted network connectivity across zones, leading to service outages and increased latency for affected GCP products.
mitigation_principle: review power distribution design to add protections against voltage swells/sags; reconfigure UPS voltage regulator with monthly reviews; deploy double‑conversion UPS for critical equipment; optimize network device configurations to reduce recovery time; verify risk does not exist elsewhere; investigate manual recovery requirements

original_source: Cloud Customers may experience minimal service disruption in us-east5-c
failure_pattern: A maintenance activity in the us-east5-c zone disrupted the zone’s network fabric, causing increased latency and packet loss for a subset of traffic. This degradation affected VM‑to‑VM, ingress, and egress paths, impacting Compute Engine, Persistent Disk, VPC, GKE, and TPU instances while new VMs were redirected to other zones.
mitigation_principle: perform maintenance with real‑time traffic monitoring; isolate maintenance to non‑critical zones; redirect workloads proactively; implement automated rollback if performance degrades; maintain detailed change logs; conduct post‑maintenance verification tests

original_source: Multiple GCP Products including Google Cloud Networking, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Cloud Load Balancing are experiencing issues in the asia-southeast2 region
failure_pattern: A latent software defect in a backbone networking router, combined with two prior fiber failures, exhausted reserve network capacity buffers, leading to loss of inter-region connectivity and causing high latency, elevated error rates, and failures across multiple GCP services.
mitigation_principle: Enhance network observability and real-time monitoring; implement automated failover and redundancy for backbone routers; conduct rigorous regression testing of router firmware; establish proactive maintenance and repair schedules with fiber partners; refine incident response playbooks and emergency tools

original_source: Multiple GCP products impacted in us-west2 region / us-west2-a zone
symptoms: inability to create or modify resources
failure_pattern: A configuration mismatch between two components of the internal cluster management system disabled a critical dependency for infrastructure services, causing the cluster service discovery component to fail. The failure prevented services from locating each other, leading to API failures, VM unavailability, and other downstream outages across the us‑west2 region.
mitigation_principle: implement automated configuration validation; use versioned configuration management; perform impact analysis before rollouts; pause rollouts of critical components until validated; add health checks for cluster service discovery

original_source: Multiple Google Cloud Products are experiencing issues in us-west1
symptoms: high error rates in predictions and training
failure_pattern: An unexpected spike in demand on the regional metadata store exceeded its capacity to provision resources, causing elevated latencies and errors that propagated through the control plane of many services. The resulting control plane unavailability led to API errors, timeouts, and failures across compute, networking, and data services in us-west1.
mitigation_principle: implement proactive traffic monitoring and alerting; enable automated throttling of workloads during spikes; enhance capacity scaling for metadata store

original_source: Multiple cloud products are experiencing network connectivity issues. New instances of several cloud products will come up without a network in many regions.
failure_pattern: A refactor in the maintenance automation omitted a zone‑scoping parameter, causing the shutdown command to target all VPC controllers instead of a single zone. The disabled safeguard allowed the operation to proceed, leading to a global shutdown of VPC controllers. The loss of VPC controllers caused the networking control plane to fail, resulting in new instances being launched without network connectivity and widespread service disruptions.
mitigation_principle: enforce mandatory zone specification in automation scripts; implement automated safety checks to reject multi‑zone operations without explicit scope; restrict access to maintenance operations; conduct comprehensive positive and negative testing of safeguards; monitor for unexpected shutdowns

original_source: Multiple product outage in europe-west8-b
failure_pattern: During a planned networking upgrade, technicians inadvertently unplugged production fiber connections adjacent to those scheduled for removal, isolating part of the europe-west8-b zone from the backbone network. This isolation cut off connectivity for VMs, persistent disks, and network services, causing widespread unavailability of compute, storage, and networking products in the zone.
mitigation_principle: pause similar global maintenance work; implement automated notifications; batch execution; enforce operational supervision; perform multi‑step traffic verification before disconnections; add procedural controls for critical tasks

original_source: Multiple services impacted in australia-southeast1.
failure_pattern: An undervoltage event at the third‑party data center caused power loss, which triggered overcurrent trips on the ATS units. Because the ATS trip settings were incorrectly configured, the redundant power paths failed, leading to loss of power to the affected racks and causing outages across multiple services.
mitigation_principle: audit and update ATS trip settings to match site design; perform comprehensive operational procedure audit; coordinate with utility provider to understand power events

original_source: Some VPC users experienced multiple issues in northamerica-northeast2-c zone
symptoms: new VMs failing to reach Google-hosted services
newly created VMs unable to reach VMs in other regions
failure_pattern: A brief power interruption to backbone networking equipment serving the northamerica-northeast2-c zone caused a loss of connectivity for VPC users. As a result, newly created VMs could not reach Google-hosted services or communicate with VMs in other regions.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant power supplies for backbone equipment; add health checks for network connectivity; enable automatic failover for critical network paths; conduct regular power outage drills

original_source: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) customers located in us-central1 may observe an issue with VPC Service Controls for newly created VMs or networks.
symptoms: requests denied by VPC Service Controls for newly created VMs or networks
Private Google Access failures for non-RFC1918 private networks
failure_pattern: When new VMs or networks were created, the VPC network data was not yet propagated to the VPC Service Controls system. As a result, API calls originating from those resources lacked the necessary network context, causing VPC Service Controls to incorrectly deny access. This also impacted Private Google Access for non‑RFC1918 private networks.
mitigation_principle: implement robust metadata propagation mechanisms; add health checks for network data availability before API calls; enforce automated testing of new VM/network creation flows; monitor propagation latency and alert on delays; add fallback logic for missing network data

original_source: [Cloud CDN, Cloud Load Balancing, Hybrid Connectivity] elevated latency in the UK (europe-west2)
root_cause_category: power outage due to substation switchgear failure
failure_pattern: A substation switchgear failure caused loss of primary and backup power feeds to a London POP, shutting down Google Front Ends (GFEs) and networking equipment. This triggered BGP route withdrawals and delayed convergence, leading to elevated latency, timeouts, and connection failures for services relying on those GFEs.
mitigation_principle: enhance power redundancy and automatic failover; improve automation of recovery processes; increase control plane resilience for interconnect; perform thorough root cause analysis with equipment vendors

original_source: Customers are experiencing connectivity issues with multiple Google Cloud services in zone us-east5-c
symptoms: temporary errors in IAM, KMS, and Secret Manager
prolonged outages for Cloud Filestore and Persistent Disk
failure_pattern: Utility power loss in us‑east5‑c triggered UPS failure due to battery failure, causing loss of power to virtual machine instances and infrastructure. Without power, compute, storage, and networking services became unavailable or degraded, leading to high latency, failed failovers, and connectivity loss.
mitigation_principle: implement redundant power paths with automatic failover; harden UPS battery health monitoring; audit systems lacking automatic failover; test generator handover procedures; collaborate with UPS vendor to remediate battery backup issues

original_source: We are investigating elevated error rates with multiple products in us-east1
symptoms: service disruptions in Gmail, Drive, Meet, Chat, Calendar, Docs, Groups, Voice
failure_pattern: During a planned hardware replacement, engineers mistakenly disconnected the active network switch that served the control plane instead of the redundant unit, while the redundant unit was also de‑configured. This caused a control plane partition, and a subsequent topology change in the fail‑open state propagated stale routing information, leading to packet loss and increased latency across GCP and GWS services in us‑east1.
mitigation_principle: implement safety controls before non‑critical hardware upgrades; enforce strict disconnection procedures for active network devices; design fail‑over mechanisms to prevent control plane partitioning during dual upstream router failures

original_source: reCAPTCHA Enterprise elevated error rate issue
failure_pattern: A recent update to the reCAPTCHA Enterprise client library incorrectly directed requests to customer servers instead of Google's reCAPTCHA servers. This caused the customer servers to receive unexpected requests to non-existent URIs, resulting in 404 errors and disabling reCAPTCHA functionality for affected users.
mitigation_principle: rigorous client-side code testing; thorough validation of request routing before deployment; comprehensive code review for external-facing libraries

original_source: Multiple GCP products are experiencing Service issues.
root_cause_category: software bug causing null pointer exception
failure_pattern: A code change in Service Control omitted proper error handling and lacked a feature flag. When a policy update with blank fields was applied, a null pointer exception caused the Service Control binary to crash globally. The crash propagated through replicated metadata, leading to 503 errors across GCP services.
mitigation_principle: modularize critical services to fail open; enforce feature flags for all critical changes; implement incremental global data replication; improve error handling and testing; adopt randomized exponential backoff; ensure monitoring infrastructure remains available during outages
